1) blood pressure rhythms are common in children, and 2) children who exhibit these rhythms tend to be taller and weigh more.
3-hour rhythms in blood pressure were present in 62 percent of children 7 to 10 years old.

1) the rhythms in systolic blood pressure are ultradian with a 3-hour cycle, 2) children of hypertensive parents do not differ from children of normotensive parents in the presence or absence of significant blood pressure rhythmicity, 3) the presence or absence and the amplitude of blood pressure rhythmicities in children is associated with height and weight.

the relationship between blood pressure (BP) rhythms, age, gender, and race in children.
the development of a new method for the measurement of blood pressure in children and the application of this method to the study of blood pressure rhythms.
the development of blood pressure rhythms in early school‐age children and the relationship between rhythmicity and other factors such as age, gender, and parental blood pressures.

children of normotensive parents have blood pressure rhythms similar to those of children of hypertensive parents.

the majority of healthy children have significant blood pressure rhythms.

children of hypertensive parents have no more significant blood pressure rhythms than do children of normotensive parents.
